definition: Preparatory set is the pattern of neural readiness or planning that develops before an action is carried out. In this source, it refers to differences in brain activity during the preparation phase before pro- versus anti-saccadic eye movements.

reasons: The definition’s general description of “pattern of neural readiness or planning that develops before an action is carried out” is not explicitly supported in the provided packet text.

The packet supports only that fMRI BOLD responses during a “preparatory period” differed for anti- versus pro-saccades and were interpreted as reflecting “differences in preparatory-set,” not the broader “neural readiness/planning” wording or the “before an action is carried out” framing.

The definition generalizes beyond the packet: the source only supports ‘preparatory set’ in the specific context of pro- and anti-saccade preparation, not as a general term for neural readiness before any action.

The phrase ‘pattern of neural readiness or planning’ is broader and more abstract than the source’s wording, which describes elevated BOLD response during the preparatory phase and interprets it as differences in preparatory planning.
The second sentence is supported only as an application to anti- versus pro-saccadic eye movements, so the broader opening sentence should not be presented as the term’s general meaning.
